name: Responses API — direct (no agent)
summary: POST /openai/v1/responses with model='{conn}/{deployment}' and no agent_reference.
description: `aoai.responses.create(model='{connection}/{deployment}', ...)` calls the Foundry project OpenAI Responses API without an agent wrapper. This is the baseline BYOM route that proves the APIM AI Gateway prefix works before layering Prompt Agents or tools on top.
notes:
Foundry emulates the Responses API on top of Chat Completions: state is stored pre-translation in a true Responses shape, but every actual model call is downconverted to `/chat/completions` before it leaves the service. Anything the model itself needs to see as Responses (reasoning items, `web_search_preview`, `computer_use_preview`, etc.) cannot round-trip.

**State layer (works).** All four persistence surfaces succeed with a BYOM-prefixed create, verified 2026-07-17 on `resp_03c8b3bc95…`:
- `aoai.responses.create(model='{conn}/{deployment}', instructions=…, input=…)` — returns a Response object.
- `aoai.responses.retrieve(id)` — returns the stored response with the original `instructions` field intact and `model` still holding the full `{conn}/{deployment}` prefix (i.e. state is stored **before** the chat translation).
- `aoai.responses.input_items.list(id)` — returns the original `ResponseInputMessageItem`s.
- `aoai.responses.create(previous_response_id=id, …)` — the follow-up correctly recalled the marker from turn 1.
- `aoai.responses.delete(id)` — succeeds; the next retrieve returns a proper 404 `Response with id '…' not found.`

**Translation layer (verified in APIM).** Two probe calls (basic + `instructions=`) both arrived at the APIM upstream as:

> `POST https://apim-ai-3swd46vd3j22a.azure-api.net/inference/deployments/gpt-4o-mini/chat/completions?api-version=2025-03-01-preview`

not `/responses`. Captured request body:

> `{"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Today Date: 18 July 2026\n\nImage input capabilities: Enabled"}, {"type": "text", "text": "You are a marker echoer. Always reply with exactly the marker: APIMPROBE2ce055a92"}]}, {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "what is the marker?"}]}], "stream": true, "max_completion_tokens": 16384, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}, "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 1.0}`

What Foundry does at execution time:
- Rewrites the path from `/openai/v1/responses` to `/inference/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions`.
- Strips the `{conn}/` prefix from `model` in the body and moves the full prefix to the `x-ms-foundry-model-id` request header.
- Converts the Responses top-level `instructions=` into a `role: system` chat message.
- Injects an extra system preamble (`Today Date: … \n\n Image input capabilities: Enabled`).
- Forces `stream: true` and `max_completion_tokens: 16384` regardless of what the caller passed.

**Impact.** Model-native Responses-only features that Foundry cannot express in a chat/completions body — reasoning items with encrypted content, `web_search_preview` / `computer_use_preview` tools, Responses-shape event streams — will not work through this endpoint even when the upstream model supports them. Chat-shaped completions (system/user/assistant messages, standard tool calls) round-trip cleanly. Callers should treat this as "Chat Completions with a Responses-shaped state API at the edge", not a true Responses passthrough.

**Ownership model (no per-response ACL).** The stored response has no `owner`, `created_by`, `principal_id`, or similar identity field — only caller-supplied `user` / `safety_identifier` / `metadata`, all `null` by default. Empirically confirmed 2026-07-17 by creating a response as my user identity and then, with a **freshly-created service principal that has only `Foundry User` on the Foundry account and had never seen the response before**, calling `responses.retrieve(id)`, `responses.input_items.list(id)`, and `responses.delete(id)` — all three succeeded, and the subsequent user-side retrieve returned `HTTP 404 Response with id '...' not found.`. Access is gated entirely by project-scope RBAC: any identity with `Foundry User` (or higher) on the account can read AND destructively delete any other identity's stored responses. Do not treat Foundry-stored responses as caller-private.

Still the control path for Prompt Agent tests: failures here point at the Chat Completions upstream, while failures above it point at the agent or tool layer.
